arguments.value: Andrew Lamar Carter, Jr., born in 1969 in Albany, Georgia, is a United States District Judge for the Southern District of New York. He was nominated by President Barack Obama on May 19, 2011, to a seat vacated by Victor Marrero, confirmed by the Senate on December 5, 2011, and received his commission on December 8, 2011. Before joining the district court, he served as a U.S. Magistrate Judge for the Eastern District of New York from 2009 to 2011. He earned a B.A. from the University of Texas in 1991 and a J.D. from Harvard Law School in 1994. Earlier in his career, he worked as a program assistant at the Ford Foundation from 1994 to 1996, as a staff attorney at the Legal Aid Society in New York City from 1996 to 2005, and as an attorney with the Federal Defenders of New York from 2005 to 2009, including service as a supervising attorney.
